criterion: The sequence sits on one near-black ground, and a single pale green appears only on an interactive element and on the studio's contact address.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the whole sequence shares one near-black ground and the pale green is worn only by interactive elements and the contact address; answer no when a second accent colour owns any other surface.

criterion: Depth on the case stack comes from the graded veil over each card, with every surface in the sequence otherwise flat.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the stack reads as depth through its veils alone; answer no when a drop shadow or a raised border carries depth anywhere in the sequence.

criterion: Display headings overlap vertically, caption blocks read as tight uppercase runs, and body copy is the one register set for continuous reading.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the three type registers behave that way on the home sequence; answer no when display lines sit apart or caption blocks read as running prose.

criterion: Every state change on every control in the sequence moves at one shared speed.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when hovering different controls produces the same timing; answer no when one control animates at a visibly different speed from the others.

criterion: A block on the sequence arrives once on the way down and holds its arrived state when the reader scrolls over the block a second time.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when scrolling over a block a second time leaves the block in place; answer no when the entrance replays on the way back down.

criterion: Under a reduced motion preference the starburst holds still, both text bands hold still, and every entrance resolves at once to its end state.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the preference stills the continuous movement and resolves entrances immediately; answer no when the starburst or a band keeps moving under it.

criterion: The studio console reads quiet and dense, built for scanning a queue and repeating an action.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the console is a plain working surface with rows tight enough to scan; answer no when it borrows the public sequence's oversized headings or atmosphere.

criterion: Body text on the sequence reaches a contrast ratio of 4.5 to 1 against the ground behind the copy.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when body copy measured against its ground meets that ratio; answer no when any body copy falls below it.

criterion: Every focusable element in the console and on the sequence wears a visible focus ring.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when tabbing through both surfaces keeps a visible ring on the focused element; answer no when the ring disappears on any control.

criterion: Every gesture on the archive wall has a keyboard equivalent that reaches the same item.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the arrow keys pan the wall and the enter key opens the focused item; answer no when the wall can only be worked with a pointer.

criterion: The composition changes once, around the width of a tablet held upright, and holds at every width between the named steps.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when one width carries the layout change and the pages hold either side of it; answer no when the layout breaks at a width between the steps.

criterion: Below that width the hero display lines stop overlapping and drop to heading size with the statement beneath them.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the narrow hero stacks its lines at heading size; answer no when the display lines keep overlapping on a handset.

criterion: The band across the top of the document repeats its text as one continuous run over a two minute watch.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the band shows no join over that watch; answer no when a gap or a repeat edge appears in the run.

criterion: Pointing at a link in the sequence tears its label into two offset copies that separate and re-converge as the label turns to the one pale green the product wears for a pointed-at state.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the tear happens on the menu, the contact address and the footer list alike; answer no when a link only changes colour.

criterion: On a coarse pointer the system pointer stays in place and every control remains usable.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a touch device keeps its own pointer and every control still works; answer no when the replacement rings are mounted on a touch device.

criterion: The sequence holds its position under an open overlay and becomes scrollable again once the last overlay has closed.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when opening and closing two overlays in an overlapping order leaves the sequence scrollable; answer no when the page stays locked after the last one closes.

criterion: The ground behind the sequence is a lit cloth whose folds catch a moving light, and every block stays readable when that surface is absent.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the folds light up under a moving pointer and the copy survives the surface being switched off; answer no when the ground is a flat image or the copy disappears with the surface.

criterion: The arrival counter climbs to one hundred in step with what has actually loaded, moving upward at every reading.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the count tracks real loading and only ever rises; answer no when the count runs on a fixed duration or slips backwards.

criterion: A key press during the arrival sequence completes the arrival at once, and the two bottom statements stay in the positions already held.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a key press lands the reader on a usable page with those two lines unmoved; answer no when the key press is ignored or the two lines jump.

criterion: The product steps its own quality down under a slow frame rate and holds the lower step for the rest of the visit.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a throttled session drops an effect and stays dropped; answer no when the effects return while the session is still slow.
